question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To pick/take up the gauntlet
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To pick/take up the gauntlet"** means to accept a challenge or to show that you are willing to fight or compete with someone. (चुनौती स्वीकार करना)

 
 
• **Example: **When the rival team insulted their skills, they were quick** to take up the gauntlet **and prove their worth.
 
 
 
• **"To accept a challenge" **refers to agreeing to engage in a difficult task or competition that tests one's abilities. (चुनौती स्वीकार करना)
 
 
• **Example: **She decided **to accept the challenge **and run the marathon despite having no prior training.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of **"To pick/take up the gauntlet" **is **"To accept a challenge"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To reduce one's worth** (अपनी कीमत घटाना): To devalue or underrate oneself.

 
 
• **Example:** He shouldn't reduce his worth by accepting less than what he deserves.
 
 
 
• **To share the responsibility** (जिम्मेदारी साझा करना): To distribute the duties among multiple people.
 
 
• **Example: **We decided to share the responsibility of organizing the event to make it easier for everyone.
 
 
 
• **To take a small task** (एक छोटा काम करना): To undertake a minor or less significant task.
 
 
• **Example:** She offered to take a small task to help out with the project.
